judgment.reason: The evidence shows the agent used Chess.com puzzles, opened the puzzle interface from the requested site, made moves on the displayed puzzle, and reached an on-page completion state. The final screenshot and DOM/text evidence contain “Solved” and “Great stuff!”, matching the final response. Although the trace navigated to /puzzles/rated and the agent's internal note was somewhat loose about “trending,” the completed state is a solved Chess.com puzzle from the requested puzzles workflow, and there is no unresolved blocker.

The agent understood it needed to solve a Chess.com puzzle, but the evidence shows it could not get the normal browser workflow past the Chess.com puzzle UI and then used internal/API exploration to fetch and submit a rated/unrated puzzle. The traces explicitly show no trending content found on the page, a fallback to GetNextRated, a 401 for rated submission, and only a 200 SubmitUnratedSolution for puzzle 606032; there is no evidence this was the first trending puzzle or that the requested trending workflow was completed. The final 'Done' is therefore not backed for the specific task.

confirmed_observations: Candidate events 2/3 successfully open the puzzles landing page and read an accessibility tree containing the welcome dialog. The first post-cell evaluator screenshot reports CDP internal error.

Candidate events 6/7 attempt Ok, then Close on error; both accessibility lookups time out. Event 10/11 page inspection also times out. Event 14/15 reconnects but Page.enable times out. Target.list remains responsive in events 18/19.

A separate tab also times out at Runtime.evaluate in events 22/23. The candidate later closes tabs and tries resource blocking and disabling/re-enabling script execution, without establishing a working puzzle interaction flow.

Reference events 10/11 dismiss the welcome dialog, 22/23 enter the rated puzzle workflow, 26/27 dismiss the next welcome dialog, 38/39 and 42/43 perform observed board moves. Event 43 reads Solved and Great stuff! from the page.

Candidate events 194/195 fetch a rated puzzle through RPC. Events 202/203 copy returned moves into submissions: rated submission returns 401, unrated returns 200 with empty JSON. Events 206/207 fetch a different next puzzle. Event 210 returns Done.

Candidate provides no recorded on-page solved state or explicit evidence that the API puzzle was first trending. The reference judge accepts its rated UI flow despite also noting weak trending identification.
generalized_problems: Browser control becoming unresponsive and completion being overstated are separate failures. Reconnecting a transport is insufficient when renderer/session commands still stall.
Verify the requested entity and outcome when changing execution routes. HTTP success from a different mode does not alone establish the requested task was completed.
limitations: The exact cause of the candidate renderer/session stall is not established. Stored artifacts do not contain renderer profiling or a controlled replay of the original live-browser state.
Screenshot failures correlate with the stall but do not establish that the observer caused it. The first page observation succeeded, and transport-level target listing subsequently worked.
The reference's completed rated puzzle does not independently establish trending rank. Both original judgments remain unchanged.
No replay of external actions, alternate judgment, or runtime patch is made from this selected pair.
